backend_calls.notes: Mostly fixed vocabulary that a dictionary can translate: sign names, planet names (some end in ' (yaklaşık)'), aspects (Kavuşum/Üçgen/Sekstil/Kare/Karşıt/Quincunx), elements, house systems (Placidus/Koch/Eşit Ev/Tam Burç/'Porphyry (yüksek enlem)'). lib/mcp-dil.js already has TR->EN for all of these. FREE-FORM TURKISH PROSE that a dictionary cannot handle: (1) gezegenler[].yorum = noktaYorumu() from lib/nokta-yorum.js plus 517 KB lib/yorumlar.json (baslik/soru/burcMetni/evMetni). There is no English version anywhere, and the MCP English path does not interpret either. Workaround: the page already has a fallback for p.yorum==null (gezegenDetay lines 595-598, using the client-side PL/BURC/EV/ACI dictionaries), so the EN page can ignore p.yorum and translate those dictionaries. English interpretations will be thinner than the Turkish ones. (2) `not` (no-birth-time warning) is Turkish; replace it with English when dogumBilgi.saatBilinmiyor is true (NOT.saatYok.en exists in mcp-dil.js). (3) `cark` SVG has a Turkish title ('Doğum Haritası', wheel.js:73) and legend ('Üçgen, Sekstil, Kare, Karşıt, retro, ek noktalar', wheel.js:268-273). Fix by string-replacing inside the <text> nodes on the client, or with a tiny backend change: pass aciAdlari('en') and BASLIK.harita.en, which lib/mcp.js:424 already does for ChatGPT. data-ad/data-a attributes stay Turkish and work as internal keys. (4) dogumBilgi.tarih is 'DD.MM.YYYY' (fmtTarihTR, server.js:1132); reformat it on the client from the ISO input. (5) dogumBilgi.yer comes back in Turkish because geo.js searches with language=tr ('Londra, Birleşik Krallık'); show the user's English autocomplete label instead. (6) BUG RISK: if geocode finds no match it silently falls back to 'Ankara (varsayılan)' with Europe/Istanbul (geo.js:5). The EN page must detect '(varsayılan)' in yer and show an error. (7) Error messages are Turkish: 429 mesaj, 400 errors[], 500 mesaj. Map them by HTTP status to English strings. Recommended small backend change: a `dil:'en'` flag that reuses mcp-dil.js (wheel legend/title, translated names, English not/errors, skip noktaYorumu to cut payload, error instead of Ankara fallback).

rationale: Include it in phase 1, but as a trimmed v1. This is the hub tool: 'birth chart calculator', 'natal chart', 'free birth chart' and 'birth chart' are among the highest-volume astrology queries in English. Every other EN tool page (rising sign, moon sign, etc.) will want a 'see your full chart' link, so an EN section without it would feel hollow. Be honest about ranking: competition is extreme (astro-seek, cafeastrology, astrology.com, astro-charts, Co-Star/CHANI apps, plus the large reference site we must never name), so a new /en/ subfolder will almost certainly not rank for the head terms soon. Realistic wins are long-tail angles the page really has: one-tap house-system comparison that shows which planets change house (Placidus/Koch/Equal/Whole Sign), an intercepted-sign explanation, an interactive filterable wheel with PNG download, and 'teach your AI your chart' text export. Feasibility is good because the calculation is universal (Swiss Ephemeris, IANA timezones) and the returned data is mostly fixed vocabulary that lib/mcp-dil.js already translates. Caveats that make it large and medium-risk: (a) about 1,390 visible words plus about 200 words of JSON-LD, and about 210 unique Turkish JS literals (about 1,150 words); roughly 55 of those are vocabulary keys, the rest sentences built with Turkish grammar by concatenation (e.g. lines 597, 616, 714-721). (b) The JS logic keys on Turkish names from the backend: ASP_COLOR/ASP_GLYPH, filter data-f='Kavuşum', ANA list, gezegenBul('Güneş'), indexOf('Düğüm'), /Placidus|Koch/, /Tam Burç/, ' (yaklaşık)'. Translation must be a display-only layer (t(name)); search-and-replace would break filters, highlighting and element counts. (c) Rich per-planet interpretations (yorumlar.json, 517 KB Turkish prose) cannot be used. Force the existing short client-side fallback text (PL/BURC/EV/ACI, about 60 strings), so EN interpretations will be modest and the selling point is the chart itself, not readings. (d) Drop asteroids/fixed stars (Turkish prose from the backend). (e) Fix the wheel SVG title/legend (client string-replace, or ideally a small `dil:'en'` flag on /api/harita reusing mcp-dil.js the way lib/mcp.js:424 already does), and guard the silent Ankara geocode fallback. (f) Remove the 10 paid-report touchpoints listed. With those cuts the build is about 1-1.5 days and worth it as the cornerstone of the EN section; if phase 1 must be only quick wins, it is the one large item to schedule deliberately rather than skip.
